utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies, sir. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would need the assistance of the usher to show the Court and my colleagues from the Prosecution and the witness the rest of the documents that I intend to use in my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I take it, Ms. Residovic, you may not finish by 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Your Honour, your estimate is quite correct. However, as you see, certain things happen in an unforeseeable way and we cannot entirely follow the schedule, and I hope you will be accommodating, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, you remember that we left off yesterday on the events before the assembly of Macedonia on the 25th and 26th of June and the measures that the police force of Skopje in the Republic of Macedonia took to protect the Albanian population in one part of the town. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you kindly look at this second set of documents, behind tab 34.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's exhibit 1D131. We need page N005-1053. In English it is N005-1053-ET.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have this document before you?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the top, it says that it's a document of the MVR of the Republic of Macedonia, Skopje city, internal affairs sector. Look at the document. Tell me, who drafted this information?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information was prepared by the department for analysis at the SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what is this report about?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I already mentioned, in the previous session, that on that particular date, there were major demonstrations in front of the assembly of the Republic of Macedonia caused by our obligation to facilitate a corridor; that is to say, to end the armed clashes in Aracinovo and to allow the terrorists to leave the village. This decision --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We heard that yesterday. Just tell me, does this report deal with the events of that day, as you testified yesterday?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you kindly look behind tab 35.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's exhibit 1D130, page 1D4320, and 1D4322 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, who drafted it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information was drafted by the analytical services at the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, does this report also describe the events you testified about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I'm able to see, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have explained the reasons for that clash yesterday, but you also said that the police of Skopje, in 2001, faced other protests by citizens. Do you remember saying that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Throughout the whole period of the crisis, there were constant protests by dissatisfied citizens.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned yesterday the events around Tetovo. What about them? Did they also reflect on the security situation in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very often, not even on a daily basis, the population from Tetovo protested also in front of the assembly of the Republic of Macedonia. One cannot say that this was just people from Skopje therefore. They came from all areas under threat. There was constant presence of population dissatisfied by the measures that the MOI was undertaking to suppress terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look behind 36.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's exhibit 1D128. Macedonian is 1D4 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch all the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D4295 is Macedonian, and 1D4298 is English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, we have another report here. Do you know who drafted this one?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This information was drafted by the analytics section at the SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it's the sector of internal affairs where you discharged the functions of the assistant chief for crime police?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the subject of this report, it says: "The protest of the residents of villages of Tetovo; many facilities and OSCE vehicles were damaged." Does this report indicate what you just said, that people, residents of other places also came to Skopje to demonstrate?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think this information reflects this. These were very tense situations, whereby part of the citizens expressed a revolt also through attacks or damaging facilities in ownership of Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to look behind 37.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's exhibit 1D126. Page 1D4043 in Macedonian, and 1D4046 ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I ask any further questions, could you tell me, since you were the chief of crime police for Skopje, did competent authorities of the SVR and MVR, that is OVR, try to enforce the law; that is, to detect perpetrators of crimes that were committed during such demonstrations in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, the obligation, in circumstances such as these, was related to public peace and order. However, when we have also criminal offences being committed, the obligation of the crime police is to become involved and to try to clear up these cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, since the subject of this report is that persons guilty of disturbing public law and order and theft on the given date were detected, what does it show?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It provides an overview of the activities undertaken for uncovering the perpetrators of criminal offences; that is to say, as far as I can remember, we had brought in over 50 people. For at least 30, we were able to prove that they had committed criminal offences, and they were, of course, processed before the competent authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said, a moment ago, that property was frequently threatened. As far as you know, the perpetrators in these demonstrations were endangering whose property?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They threatened property which they believed was owned by Albanians, which, in most cases, was so. However, as police, we cannot separate citizens. They all have the right to the same kind of protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you said, in view of this report and the occasion of one such demonstration, you had identified over 50 persons and took them into custody. Who were they by ethnicity, overwhelmingly? Who were the persons you brought in and possibly took other measures?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly, they were young people of Macedonian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask for pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you kindly look at tab 39.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's exhibit 1D129.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Again, who wrote this report, Mr. Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information again originates from, or rather, is prepared by the department for analysis at the SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this report, too, confirm, as you testified, that demonstrations happened almost daily with security repercussions in the city?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe not a single day went by without protests, during which the citizens expressed their dissatisfaction by attacks of facilities owned by Albanians but also by attacks and damage of property belonging to international organisations. They felt that they were responsible for part of the events in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please look at tab 41.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's exhibit 1D127. The number is N004-9837, and the English version is 9837 to 9840-ET.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have the document?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who wrote this report?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The department for analysis at the SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this report, too, dealing with the protest of citizens of Skopje, damaging -- causing great damage to various buildings confirm your prior testimony?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps the cause of the protest was somewhat different. Here we had a case of revolt of citizens provoked by the incident in the village of Ljuboten; that is to say, the terrorist attack that cost the lives of eight members of the Macedonian army. This was an extremely large protest. The masses did not stay just in front of the assembly but also moved through the city streets, and many -- and many criminal offences were noted then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now turn to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] N004-9838 in Macedonian. In English, I believe it's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It begins with: "Otherwise due to disrupting of public law and order damage of stores ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we find that part in the English version also? This could be the same page, a few paragraphs above. That means the previous page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, I'll read because it's the page before in Macedonian: "Otherwise due to participation in public law and order or damage of stores and other business facilities as well as theft, about a total of 46 people were brought in, in police stations Centar, Bit Pazar, and Kisela Voda, out of which 23 were minors. Interviews were conducted with them, whereby it was established that 32 of them committed theft and damaged facilities." Does this part of the report confirm what you just said; namely, that around 50 persons were brought in that day?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We undertook measures to that end; although, I must say that the number of criminal offences committed was high and we could not prevent it, because we were also engaged in preventing an interethnic clash between the Macedonians and Albanians. Again, we had to establish our priorities in this regard; but after the tensions were calmed, we immediately undertook actions to find the perpetrators and to bring them in.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the passage I just read, it says that steps were taken, they were brought to the police stations of Centar, Bit Pazar, and Kisela Voda. Does this sentence corroborate your testimony yesterday as to who was in charge of taking steps when there are suspicions that a crime was committed and some people are suspected of committing them?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Department of the Interior in the area of which the crimes occurred.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we turn to the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As we see on this page, we have a large number of businesses listed, those that were damaged or looted during the protests. If you look at the list of businesses, do we see that most of them belonged to Albanians?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Most of these businesses do belong to owners of Albanian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to the document we looked at a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's exhibit 1D126. It is at tab 42.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And here, too, we have a long list of names, if you look from page 1043 in Macedonian and 1046 [as interpreted] in English, up to 1045 in Macedonian and 1D4047 in English. A large number of persons are listed here, the last number being 30. Tell me, did these police stations, in fact, succeed in identifying some of the perpetrators of crimes, and is this the list of persons identified as such?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This information lists the persons who were uncovered as perpetrators of criminal offences. The police stations acted within their competencies; and in view of the fact that these offences happened on the territory of OVR Centar, as part of their activities, they submitted or filed the relevant criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we now look together at the document at tab 43.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's 65 ter 406, N004-9844; and in English, it's 9844 to 45-ET.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, who drafted this report?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one, too, was prepared by the department for analysis at the SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We read here about a vigorous action by the MVR to prevent things from escalating into vandalism. Does this also deal with one of the protests by citizens and the efforts of the police of SVR Skopje to prevent these people from committing crimes?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were continuing, ongoing activities, by which we tried to protect the property of persons and the perpetration of criminal offences.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to take now the third set of documents, which is not large. We could look at a couple of documents only, and then we'll return to the documents we discussed now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Show first, please, the document at tab 173. That's 65 ter 1D1219.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is this document, Mr. Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Behind tab 173. Did you manage to find this document? You see it on the screen also.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document. This is a criminal report filed against four persons for theft during the protests. This criminal report was filed by the relevant department of the interior, because these crimes were committed on the territory of OVR Centar. It was they who undertook measures and activities for uncovering these persons and filing the criminal report as part of their regular activities.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness to pause before answering his question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, we were cautioned by the interpreters to make pauses between question and answer?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise if I was speaking too quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that it was filed by a competent body organ of internal affairs. Where do you see in this report the note on which is the competent organ of internal affairs that filed this report?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this criminal report --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Who is the title of this criminal report, if you are able to say that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this criminal report, we can see that it was prepared by the department for internal affairs, Skopje, OVR Skopje [as interpreted], who are responsible for this case, having in mind that these offences happened on their territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I heard the translation "OVR Skopje," while I think you said OVR something else, because OVR Skopje I never heard you mention that before. So I kindly ask you to repeat which was the OVR that filed this criminal report?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I said that it was the OVR Centar. My apologies if I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The translation of this document is in the e-court; it is not in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We omitted this translation by mistake so I apologise to Their Honours and to my colleagues. They can see it on the screen only.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at the final page of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 1D1793.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who has signed this document?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There report is signed by the manager, the head of OVR Centar at the time, Mr. Trajkovski, as part of -- as part of his competencies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the signatory to this report corroborates your notion on who is in charge of filing a criminal report. Have I understood you well?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that this was a criminal report filed against four persons because of the protests in Skopje. Tell me, who were those persons: Aleksovski, Saso; Tripunovski, Goce; Metodijas, Miluv; and Tripunovski, Nikola? What is their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the criminal report, these are citizens of Macedonian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please now look at the document after tab 174.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter 1D1220. The Macedonian page is 1D9794. This document also has a partial translation included in this binder. This is draft translation, and it was not uploaded to the e-court because we just secured the draft translation today.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, if you look now at this criminal report, could you tell us whether it was produced by the competent bodies and which are those competent bodies, and who were the perpetrators this criminal offence that was reported?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This criminal report is filed by OVR Centar. It is drafted by the department for operative measures, activities. That's the department which carried out the criminalistic activities within the OVR. And, once again, these are perpetrators of Macedonian ethnicity. And in accordance with the rules, it is signed by the head of the OVR Centar; that is to say, the responsible OVR.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who are the injured parties, as reading from this criminal report?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. I don't know the persons. However, from this report, we can see that these are people of Macedonian ethnicity, if this is what you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Persons who are suspects in this report?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the second page, you say: "Namely, on the 8th of August, 2001, at the critical time between 2000 and 2200 hours, they went to the centre of the city, more precisely the parliament building, in order to express their protests for the deteriorated security situation in the Republic of Macedonia." So I'm interested to learn whether this criminal report was filed on the occasion of all these events that were -- that took place when the protests were taking place, those that we were looking at before?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This criminal report is also a part of these activities or related to these activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look now at the document in tab 175.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter 1D1221. Macedonian page is 1D9797. And this is, again, a translation, Your Honours, that we did not manage to upload in the e-court, but you have it in your binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, whether we have, again, a criminal report submitted by the competent body on the occasion of those same events?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the title, I can see that this is the Centar Department of the Interior, or rather the section for operative affairs, a criminal report for criminal offences of theft on the territory of OVR Centar perpetrated by three persons of Macedonian ethnicity, and also related and of the time when a large group of people were expressing their revolt due to the security situation in the Republic of Macedonia. And, lastly, we can see that it is signed by the head of the OVR Skopje, which I said was responsible -- Centar, OVR Centar, which, as I said, was the responsible OVR.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, answering one of my questions just previously, you stated that you paid no attention to the identity of the injured parties because, for you, all citizens were equal. Tell me, please, during your career and during your work in 2001, what was, as far as you know and in your opinion, what was the attitude of the SVR and especially the crime police that you headed, did it make any distinction when uncovering the crimes and perpetrators, based on the ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police must be understood as service of the citizens. It is not -- it is not to be bound by any kind of ethnic delineations. We are duty-bound to secure the same kind of protection, the same services, I would say, towards all citizens, because, ultimately, not only are we duty-bound by legal regulations to do this, but we are also paid with taxpayers' money of Macedonian [as interpreted] ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go now to another topic. You'll remember that we discussed yesterday the security situation assessment and the fact that this assessment was made by the OVRs, because they were best placed to know the situation in the field --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. May I intervene into the translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please go ahead?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in 14:7, line 14:7, it should state, and I believe I said, "all ethnicities," not just Macedonian ethnicity. I do not want to be misinterpreted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. You remember saying yesterday that the OVRs, the departments of internal affairs, were in charge of assessing the security situation during that crisis time and to establish the number of check-points within a given area, in order to be able to control the situation in the territory they covered. This would be a brief summary of our discussion yesterday. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you tell me, in these check-points, in 2001, how many people were deployed there, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, on the basis of the assessment which each OVR made for its own territory, they decided on the location and the number of employees who would be deployed there, to carry out the tasks provided for on those check-points. I could not say with certainty how many people deployed -- were deployed by the OVR, but I can give an average, at least to my understanding. There were check-points with five employees; there were check-points with 15 deployed employees. It is within this scope of numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's look at the document in tab 144, please. That is --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the previous file, the previous binder?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Let's leave aside this third binder. We just saw three criminal reports from it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is not 144, but 44; maybe I misspoke. That is Exhibit 1D182.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat it, which document we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're looking at the document after tab 44. That is Exhibit 1D182. Macedonian page is 1D1549 and the English page is 1D5152 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Macedonian page 1D5149.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what is this document and who is the body competent to issue it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an overview which was drafted as -- by OVR Cair. On the basis of their security assessment, they prepared an overview of places where there is possibilities for appearance of Albanian terrorists and buildings of vital importance which could be targeted for attacks in the area of OVR Cair; I will say it again, on the basis of their security assessment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look now at the page 1D5151.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 1D5155 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is this document, actually?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document lists the check-points, which OVR Cair established in its area. These check-points - that is to say, this document - was drafted by the deputy commander of police station Cair.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated, yesterday, that it had been possible, depending on the security situation, to modify the check-points in a given area. So could you repeat now who was in charge of performing such alterations?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assessment of the security situation are updated and adjusted to the current situation. This is normal. And once certain changes are noted, usually the commander of the police station is the one who proposes changes in the plan; and these proposal, these plans are approved by the competent head of OVR Cair, the responsible OVR for a given territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now look please at the document in tab 45.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 1D183. Page is 1D5157 in Macedonian, while the English page is 1D5160.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I ask you questions in relation to this document --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- does the OVR, regardless of whether it is the OVR Cair or any other, after establishing the security situation and after defining the number of check-points, does it inform anyone about it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In view of the security situation, as I said yesterday, in SVR Skopje, there was an operative headquarters. This amendment to the plan, which was prepared by police station Mirkovci and approved by the head of OVR Cair, was probably submitted to the headquarters of SVR Skopje, in view of the fact that the headquarters had to be informed and notified of the deployment of check-points in the area of OVR Cair, so that we could provide assistance in the case of need.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the top of the document, something is written in handwriting. Could you read that, Mr. Stojanovski, please?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says that this is addressed to "ZAM." This is an abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This is an abbreviation, probably, Deputy Pero Stojanov.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is probably addressed to me; and at that time, I was probably at the headquarters of the SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, Mr. Stojanovski, I will ask you to look at the documents that are in your set from tab 46 to tab 57; and in the next couple of minutes, could you please look carefully, first of all, at the nature of the documents, what they are about. And before I ask my question, we'll look together at the first one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's tab 46, P545.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me who issued it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order for conducting duties issued by the police station Cair. So we can see further on who were the officers that this order was pertaining to. These specific tasks are enumerated. The deadline within which they need to be performed; as well as, at the end, it says that six officers were deployed and each them had spent six hours working.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, in this last line, where we see 6 times 12, that means that with this order the police station ordered that six persons be engaged for 12 hours each. Did I understand this correctly?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You have the number of people; then the number of hours; and the total number of man hours for the people comprised by the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, I asked you a moment ago - and I'm going to ask you again - to look at documents from 46 to 57. All of them are similar orders for performing certain duties, and pay attention to the number of persons who were deployed within this time at various check-points. While you're looking at this, I will just give the numbers of the documents that you are viewing because of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P545, Exhibit P491, Exhibit 1D283, Exhibit 1D284, 65 ter 1D1149, Exhibit P539, Exhibit P540, Exhibit P492, Exhibit P538, Exhibit P160 -- no, I apologise. Maybe we need to skip P160, because this is not the same document. Exhibit P34, under seal; Exhibit P541.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Had you managed to look at it -- to look at them, rather?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I looked at the orders, and I can't see anything unusual about them. Was your question referring to --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The number of persons deployed at these check-points, is it normal? As you said, it could vary from five to 15. Did you notice any extraordinary changes in the number of persons manning check-points?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that the average number of deployed officers ranged between five and 15, but I can see here that in some situations even less people were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to observe in these orders that they relate to the 10th, 11th, and 12th August? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not pay attention to that. Just a moment, please. Yes, it is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to observe any major variations in the number of persons in relation to the days when the orders were issued?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is the usual number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I move on, I will ask you, Mr. Stojanovski, considering that we don't have official CLSS translations for these documents, to read the exact title of this order in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the title is: "Order for performing duties," if this is what you're referring to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "Order for carrying out service."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in light of what you have seen and said, could you pay attention only to these orders for carrying out service that relate to the 12th of August. Could you look at all those documents again and concentrate on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I saw the documents with the date 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you notice on these documents an increase in the number of persons manning check-points compared to the other documents? Can you conclude on that basis that something unusual was going on, in view of the normal number you testified to?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no increase in the number of persons manning the check-points. I would say it is at the minimum, rather.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who Ljupco Bliznakovski is?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bliznakovski was the assistant to the head of the SVR, Skopje, in charge of the uniformed police. We had adjacent offices, and we had held the same rank.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What would you say if anyone testified before this Court that Ljupco Bliznakovski had ordered the chief of OVR Cair to reinforce the check-points? What would you say about such an allegation?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that, to say the least, this would not really correspond to the true situation, for at least two reasons: First of all, Mr. Bliznakovski, I said already, we held the same rank, which means that he could not issue an order to the head of the OVR, on the one hand; while the second reason would be that the check-points were under the competence of the OVR, and I don't see a reason why anyone would say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now move on to another subject. I'd like to ask you about your knowledge of the events between the 10th and 12th August 2001 in the area of Cair municipality; in particular, Ljuboten village and the surrounding villages. Did you have any knowledge about the events that happened in that area on the 10th August 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the established information flow system, information on the situation and on the events were arriving to both the cabinet of the SVR Skopje and the headquarters of the SVR Skopje and also to the duty operations centre of the SVR Skopje, and I can say that I had the information and that I was relatively well-informed about what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did any particular report stick in your memory, something that you received on Friday, the 10th August? Did anything particularly memorable happen?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that was the date when, in the morning, within the area covered by OVR Cair, eight members of the army of the Republic of Macedonia were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In light of that fact that was reported to you in some way, did the police inform the judiciary; in other words, did you perform an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since after this terrorist action -- since in that terrorist action the army suffered casualties, and since this specific area was under their control, we established some contacts aiming towards performing an on-site investigation. However, the measures undertaken were undertaken by the army of the Republic of Macedonia. If memory serves, we contacted either the military police or the army command, and they stated that they would undertake measure together with the investigating judge for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in relation to these incidents, did you talk to the chief of OVR Cair?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with certainty who informed me about the incident. It is possible that it was the head, chief of the OVR Cair; and, probably, we did have communication regarding the decision who will make the on-site investigation, whether it would be the SVR Skopje with its forensic department that will assist the investigating judge, or whether it is to be done by the army. And as I said before, that was done by the army at the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, did you also learn that some armed persons had entered the village?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're speaking about --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The 10th.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're speaking about the 10th alone, yes, there were such information that individuals entered the village; although, we had previously information about their presence in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now briefly look at documents from tab 60 -- that is 59, sorry. Then 60, 61, 62, 63, 64. Then tell me, after reviewing them, if those are reports that you had available to you at the time or maybe later.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are Exhibits P158, P112, P150, P1 -- sorry, 1D145, P151, and P114, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, were these reports available to you at that time or later? Did you know about the things contained in these documents?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am familiar with the information and the materials. I can't say precisely when was the first time I saw them; but with regards to their content, yes, I'm familiar with that. That is an Official Note produced by the Mirkovci police station, which indicates that an army vehicle was hit on a mine -- by a mine and eight soldiers were killed. Then it is a telegram where the cabinet of the SVR Skopje is informed of --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, I just asked to you review the documents because they have been admitted into evidence already. I just wanted to ask you if these reports were available to you. There's no need to look into each of them individually. In relation to that day, the 10th, did the chief of OVR Cair, to the best of your recollection, talk to you about a meeting; and if he did, tell me, what was that discussion about?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that in the afternoon I was informed, or I do not know whether the word "informed" is appropriate. He phoned me and asked for my advice regarding some issue that the army was convening some working meeting. I believe that it was related to the Ljubanci village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what was your answer to the chief when he asked you about that; can you remember?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a bit unusual, the reason for him calling me. I believe that I told him that, if I were in his shoes, I would like to know what was going on in -- in the area I'm covering; and it was usual, normal, to have contacts with the army anyhow. So I could not understand the point of his phone call.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the chief of OVR Cair ever call you again, after asking you for your advice?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't state with certainty, but I believe that he did call me and said -- yes. He mentioned the army, that allegedly the army was planning some activities but also that it did not entail any obligation. No obligations relevant for us were given at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll take the first break now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We discussed a moment ago what you had learned, what information you had on the 10th of August. Tell me, please, Mr. Stojanovski, before we move on to the 11th, in the course of your work, who do you normally contact? Who are all the persons you are in touch with?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, I contact the heads of the OVR. It is usual that I contact the heads of organisational units I was superior to; further on, members of international organisations. Very often, I had many contacts with my colleagues about issues of different nature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Speaking of your contacts with chiefs of departments of internal affairs or criminal investigation sections of these departments, tell me, how many such calls did you receive at the time of crisis?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an enormous number of calls, discussions, and conversations. I believe that I had at least two hours of conversations on my cell phone, not to mention the other two phones. I had an external line, an internal line in the ministry. Indeed, an enormous number of conversations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This morning we saw documents that dealt with these events and incidents of vandalism in Skopje after the report of the killing of the soldier at Karpalak. Did that incident cause any involvement on your part; and if so, to what extent?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I believe I mentioned that the situation was extremely tense, critical; that we had very limited resources available; that the crime police was not fully staffed; and from that number, about 50 per cent had to be given as assistance to uniformed police. We faced a situation where people had to be engaged in Radusa, one of the hot spots that put one million strong city under threat to be left without water. There were daily problems in front of the assembly. We had problems with the airport because around the village of Aracinovo terrorists were noted, which could have threatened the security of the airport. Further, we had problems with the roads Skopje-Pristina, an international highway which we were duty-bound to keep open and which was -- there were many attempts to block this road because it was an international road, and KFOR also used this road for logistics for their forces in Kosovo. There were terrorist group in the city itself. They killed our police officers, whether it be in a store or on the street. I believe the situation was extremely dire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think you have sufficiently described the circumstances in which you worked; and in view of that situation, do you still remember what happened on the 11th of August that still stands out in your memory?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most major event, if I can say this, on this date was the very violent clashes in Radusa. This is a place nearby Skopje, from where the capital is -- receives its water supply. We had police forces surrounded by terrorists and under constant attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know about that incident in Radusa? Because the combat activities of the army and the police force are not strictly within your competence.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the one hand, I said that I was a member of the operative headquarters Skopje; and, on the other, I mentioned that my colleague, Bliznakovski, was next to my office. He was located in the office next to mine, and we were close by. We exchanged information. We usually knew what the other one was working, and he directly involved in this clash. Together, with the special unit, they went to Radusa in order to help the colleagues who were surrounded by terrorists at that time, and he tried to extract them. He tried to help them. I believe this was happening in the course of the whole day, and it was only by night-fall that the situation became calmer. This is when he came back to the premises of the SVR.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of what you know about the incidents of the 11th in Radusa, what would you say if it were to be established before this Court that on that day your colleague, Mr. Ljupco Bliznakovski, had attended a meeting at the command of the city, and then issued an order to the chief of OVR Cair to reinforce check-points in his area? How would you comment on that, in view of what you know about the events at the time? Would that be consistent with your information?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I explained previously that Mr. Bliznakovski --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. But in line 20, it says: [in English]... Court established that on that day ..." [Interpretation] I didn't say that the Court established anything. I said, "if it were to be established before this Court"; that is, if anyone claimed before this Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, in view of what you know from that time --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Shall I continue my answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe you should repeat, since I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I explained previously, the position of Mr. Bliznakovski did not allow him to issue orders. However, in view of the fact that I personally know where he was, this statement would most probably, would certainly be a lie.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Stojanovski, did there come a time when the chief of OVR Cair called you and asked you anything about that alleged meeting at the city command of Skopje on the 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such thing. I'm sure of this. This did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before these dates - the 10th, the 11th - or during those days, that is, within several weeks of these events or at the time of the events, did the chief of OVR Cair ever mention to you or indicate to you that he received a call at his home from Minister Ljube Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe this happened. He has not notified me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the chief of OVR Cair ever tell you or inform you or asked you for advice in relation to the alleged order of the minister that he would send to him Johan Tarculovski and that the minister told him on that occasion that he should give Johan Tarculovski anything he asks for? Were you aware of any such thing?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, allegedly the minister called the head of OVR Cair?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And told him to receive a certain person, as I said, Johan Tarculovski, and provide him with everything he asks for.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such information, I did not receive such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said, yesterday, that in practice you never heard that the minister had ever issued any order to anyone, including you; although, you were in a higher position. Is that consistent with the answer that you just gave, that you had never heard of such a thing?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my professional experience, up until now, I have no knowledge of information for this manner of communication.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Tell me, please, Mr. Stojanovski, on the 10th or the 11th, did the chief of OVR Cair ask you about anything else, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If somebody were to ask you whether they should distribute weapons to certain persons, would you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would most probably remember, because, if you forgive me, this is kind of a stupid question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why do you say it's not a normal question?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is completely outside of my competencies. Crime police and distribution of weapons, they don't go together, these two things.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If anyone claimed before this Court that you had issued an order to distribute weapons to certain persons at OVR Cair, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it's a lie.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, on the 10th or the 11th, did anyone inform you that Manager Mitevski had issued an order to distribute weapons to certain persons?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such -- I have not received such information; although, once again, I don't see the logic that the direction -- director would issue orders to that extent.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are there any regulations in the Ministry of Internal Affairs governing this matter?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are regulations. And, in addition to these regulations, there is an organisational unit which is duty-bound to carry out these regulations. I can speak about the example of SVR Skopje, where there was a department for defence preparations. This was within their competencies, and each OVR also had people who were charged with these matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If anyone claimed before this Court that Director Mitevski had issued an order to distribute weapons to certain persons and that you had agreed to that and ordered that this instruction of Director Mitevski be carried out, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I would say that, in the least, that this is a stupid assertion, because my position, as assistant, to give consent to an order of a superior, which is much higher up in the hierarchy than I am, is not logical. I don't think there is any need to comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let us move now to events of the 12th of August. On the 12th of August, did you receive any reports to the effect that something was going on in Ljuboten or the environs?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly at what time, but it was during the morning hours that I received the information that the army and police points in and around Ljuboten were attacked.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to that report, did you receive any other reports during that day?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot claim with certainty, but I believe it was the head of OVR Cair who informed me that the army had undertaken adequate activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Chief Krstevski call you again later during that week, one morning or around noon, or is it the case that you had no other calls from him?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, yes. He called regarding -- he was asking me how a report is given.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And why? Why did you ask you that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was informed by the duty centre that Mr. Boskoski, the Minister of the Interior, will be visiting this area, and he was asking me how this official report is given. This was rather funny, because, as civilian structures, we don't deal with this issue. Reporting is not part of the tasks which we have or the way we act. I suggested to him that, according to my view, it is quite sufficient that he present a brief information about the situation in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, that afternoon, did you have any contacts with the chief or did any reports reach you about what was going on in the area of OVR Cair, Ljuboten, Ljubanci, Radisani, and other places?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon, we began to receive quite some information, stating that part of the population is attempting to leave the village, and that some persons were brought in or were taken by the army and handed over to the police. I believe that there were not so much different but information of this kind as activities unfolded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: About those first reports you received, that some people were taken into custody and brought into the police station, at the time you received those first reports, was there any talk about taking some steps that are usual in the work of crime police?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the military action -- in the course of the military action, persons with weapons were imprisoned or - I don't know which term to use - were brought in or taken in. This was a situation that required the involvement of the crime police, in order to clarify the case. These persons were taken into custody in the police station Mirkovci, and the crime police of OVR Cair began working on clarifying the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What you just said, taking people into custody, starting an investigation, all that began in the OVR Cair, are all these activities normally within the purview of OVR Cair, and why was it that OVR Cair was in charge of that, if they were?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I have mentioned previously that for all activities that happened on the territory of a given OVR, it is that OVR that is duty-bound to undertake certain measures. In this case, this was an event that happened on the territory of OVR Cair; and, therefore, this was the obligation and task of that OVR to work on that case. There were no requests for assistance or support from SVR -- to SVR Skopje to help on this case. We received information that about ten persons were brought in with weapons in the police station Mirkovci, that members of the crime police of OVR Cair are already working and are interviewing some of the persons, and that some of the persons were injured and these were provided medical assistance. There was no reason for us to become involved or to secure any kind of support for them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that you received some other reports that afternoon relating to incidents at check-points or perhaps the arrest and bringing in of other persons into police stations?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The day was interesting, if I may say so, with regards to the events that took place then. I was informed that one part of the population of Ljuboten village were moving towards the check-points and trying to leave the village; and that, at the same time, the population of Ljubanci and Radisani were preparing to accost them and they did accost them, unfortunately, and there were -- there had already been incidents between them. I believe that it was then that the SVR Skopje was involved for the first time. Mr. Bliznakovski, upon the order of Mr. Galevski, who died in the meantime, as you know, he organised the involvement of the posebna unit in the resolving of these events, from the -- in order to prevent or, actually, to save the Albanian population that was leaving the village because it was accosted and ill-treated, if I may say so, by the Macedonian population. The OVR Cair was not able, having in mind its capacities, to put this under control.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding the tasks of the crime police, you said that you received certain reports as to what had been done in the Mirkovci police station and all that was usual, normal procedure, and you were not involved in any way. Now, regarding other people who were arrested, did the OVR make any requests for assistance with regard to them?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With regards to the Mirkovci police station, it was like that; but later on, the chief of the OVR Cair, I believe, although I can't say with certainty whether it was the chief of the OVR Cair or the chief of the department for operations, Mr. Josevski, informed me that there were many detained persons, and they were lacking sufficient capacities to keep them in the police stations. Also, they informed that among those persons who were brought there, there were individuals who they believed had participated in the armed activities; so terrorists, so to say, who were leaving their weapons, changing their clothes, and trying to leave that area together with the population. I established contact with the chief of the organised crime and coordination department, Mr. Bojic, and he undertook certain measures to secure a room in other police station to transfer the detainees there. I believe that I had contacts with the head of the forensic department, and I requested that he provided as many teams as possible that would make the paraffin glove tests in order to secure evidence that the OVR Cair would need later in order to verify those assertions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, that afternoon, were you aware that there were people dead in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that somewhere in the evening such information arrived. I believe it was sent from the Mirkovci police station by the duty officer. I believe that it spoke of five individuals who were allegedly killed during the fights there, and I believe that that information was processed and that the duty operations centre of SVR Skopje informed the investigating judge about that case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether an on-site investigation was carried out on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding -- as far as I know, the investigating judge, I believe, went to the OVR Cair. However, whether he went there and whether he spoke to the chief of the OVR Cair, I can't really remember. But whatever else happened, he did not accept to have an on-site investigation in such security situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you, Mr. Stojanovski, in order to move on more quickly through this examination, to look at documents starting with tab 68 to tab 80.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, this is Exhibit P155, under seal; P395; P23, under seal; P160; then P257; P160; P106, under seal; P157, under seal; P154, under seal; P155, under seal; P107, under seal; 65 ter number 488; P147.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you look at this, you see that, for the most part, these documents relate to the 12th of August, 2001. Mr. Stojanovski, now that you have reviewed a number of documents dated 12th August 2001, could you tell me whether they corroborate the information that was available to you on the 12th; and if so, to what extent; and, second, whether you had seen them before?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I skimmed through the documents now quickly, and I believe they do correspond to what I testified to previously. And with regards to where have I seen these documents, I can't be certain, since it is possible that I had seen them then, but it is also possible that I had seen them later during the work of the committee. So I couldn't say with certainty when it was that I had seen those documents for the first time, then or a bit later --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: In line 35.7, "when" instead of "where."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But as I said, I believe that these documents reflect what was also included in my testimony about these events.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You just mentioned some committee or commission. I'm not sure what you said. What was that about? You said, "during the work," as we have on the record, "of the committee." What was that about? What work and what body was it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day later, on the 13th of August, I was informed by Mr. Efremov, who was then the chief of the SVR Skopje, that the minister established a committee to investigate the events that took place at Ljuboten. I had not seen that document, and Mr. Efremov tasked me with being, in a way, the contact person for the work with the committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th, did you at all go to OVR Cair or perhaps the area where the events happened?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no need of my presence there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if anyone claimed before this Court that, on the evening of the 12th, you were at OVR Cair, would that jog your memory, that you, indeed, had gone there, or what would you say about that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true, and I don't know what were the reasons for such assertions. I couldn't comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the first time that you went to the area of Cair municipality after these events?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 14th of August. Mr. Efremov tasked me with that. And, chronologically speaking, on the 13th, in the afternoon, Mr. Efremov informed me of the existence of that committee and my duties towards that committee. And since no on-site investigation was conducted in the area of the village of Ljuboten on the previous day because of the security situation then, I believe that he had certain contacts with an MP, Mr. Fatmir Etemi, in order to bring the situation to a calm, so that we can carry out the on-site investigation in Ljuboten. And, at the same time, since the minister showed his interest in this event, he requested that I be directly physically present during the on-site investigation, so that I could have the first-hand information on the events in the village. That was probably the idea. But during the afternoon, during that communication with the MP and with the court, the evening came, darkness fell. The conditions were not proper to perform the on-site investigation, and it was decided to do it on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was the 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did the court assign a team or did you go there as well as you were assigned to by your chief?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain. I believe that Mr. Stavrev was the investigating judge, and I went to the premises of the OVR Cair, together with the forensics police team. We meet there the Chief Krstevski, and we worked in his office. I did follow the conversation. The situation was very interesting. Mr. Efremov was not present, but he contacted Mr. Ademi --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Mr. Etemi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Etemi relayed information to Mr. Efremov that it is possible to enter the village; and, at the same time, after this conversation, he would call Mr. Krstevski telling him that it was not possible to enter the village. So this all went on three or four times. After that, there was some attempts made to reach a bargain or agreement that the investigating judge would enter the village alone, that the police would not enter the village with him, but the investigating judge refused this and some sporadic fire was heard. After several hours of going towards the village, going back and forth, I believe that Mr. Etemi reported that the bodies were already buried, and the investigating judge decided that we would leave the location, that the on-site investigation would be illogical in the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Upon that decision of the investigating judge not to go in, to go back and then come back again, was the police, in any way, able to influence him?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I'm not an expert for theoretical explanation of law, but I believe I managed to explain yesterday that the investigating judge is superior in such cases, and that the police has no possibility to influence his decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please now look at tab 119.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's document 1D6. It's page N000-7350; and in English, it's 7350 to 7351.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As we can see, this is an Official Note of the Lower Court of Skopje II, the investigation department. Have you ever had occasion to see this document before?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you turn to page 2 of this document. And at the bottom of that page, you will see Investigating Judge Ognen Stavrev. Is that the judge you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I read his last name, and I believe he was the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The second paragraph of this document, it is stated: "In relation to this event, on the 12th of August that same year, the duty investigating judge, at 1730, was informed by the MOI, SVR duty operations centre, that in the area of Ljuboten and Ljubanci villages in Skopje vicinity, there were several members of the paramilitary of the Albanian terrorists killed, but no one could come close to the bodies because, at that moment, the military activities were still going on. "The investigating judge informed the deputy public prosecutor, Roska Karova, about the information received from the MOI. The investigating judge was also informed that the safety of the investigation bodies, the court, and the public prosecutor's office was not guaranteed because of the clashes that were still going on. So this is why no investigating measures were undertaken, more precisely because of the military clashes that were still going on between the above mentioned paramilitary forces and the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia. "Dr. Aleksej Duma, director of the Forensic Medicine and Criminology Institute, was informed of the situation." This report made by Judge Ognen Stavrev, is it consistent with what you know about the events of the 12th of August, 2001, in early evening hours?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regards to the events taking place and the measures taken by the duty operations centre, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please turn the first page of -- second page of this document. Would you kindly look at it. Let's not read it out loud; it is a long document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first page, please, N000-7350; and the English page is the same number, 7350-7351.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Again, this is an Official Note from the investigating unit of Basic Court Skopje, drafted on the 15th. It describes the events or measures that were taken by the investigating judge on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is written here, does it correspond to your knowledge about the events taking place then, because you, yourself, were present there at the OVR Cair?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it does correspond, except maybe I'm not sure about the segment related to the OSCE. I cannot say with certainty, but I think they visited the village somewhere in the afternoon on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, certainly in this part, speaking about the court attempting to enter and failing at that --

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This segment is as is; although, it is in an abbreviated form. There were much more games surrounding this whole issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Would you then look at the document in tab 121, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit 1D72.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the basic public prosecutor's office. The document is signed by the deputy public prosecutor, Milan Gelevski. Tell me, do you remember whether the deputy prosecutor accompanied the investigation team?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the usual practice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were any medical professionals present there during the on-site inspection on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was a doctor there, but I cannot recall the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this note correspond to your knowledge of the events that you testified about, that an attempt was made to enter the village and that due to reasons described in this Official Note, it was not possible to enter the village?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, I think it's in good order and it reflects the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, you stated that at the end you received information that the bodies were buried. So did it make any sense to then perform the on-site investigation? Based on your experience, what do you think?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With this procedure, with this act, the crime scene -- the scene of the event has changed, is changed dramatically. So, in my experience, the on-site investigation would not have the importance, and it could not provide relevant information. There would be no need for it in a -- in a changed situation to carry out an on-site investigation, such as this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at the document in tab 98.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P148. This is an Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, before you look at the contents of the document, this is an official note from the OVR-OOR Cair, so the department that verifies and uncovers events that are believed to constitute crimes. Is my understanding of this document correct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does it correspond to your testimony, that until the matter is taken by the prosecutor or the judge, that the exclusive competence belongs to the OVR?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope I was able to correctly elaborate on this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if, on the 12th, there had been some information that there were dead bodies in the village, who would be in charge of trying to arrive at information on the identity of the individuals and what has happened to them?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: OVR Cair is responsible for the area under its charge, so to say; and it is their obligation to try to secure all necessary information pertaining to the pre-criminal procedure, the preliminary procedure, or when they are acting upon the request of the public prosecutor and investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the first paragraph of this Official Note it is stated: "On the 14th of August 2001 at around 1800 hours, at the premises of the department of internal affairs OOR Cair, I have carried out a conversation with the person Sali Nimelula, born on 5 May 1964 in the village Ljuboten, residing at Kovacka Street, number 10, in Skopje..." Tell me, Mr. Stojanovski, whether this effort of the competent bodies, when they are not able to enter the village, should try to involve other persons or do they need to adhere to some patterns prescribed of conduct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One aspect is collection of information and another is undertaking measures. Where information is concerned, they can try to do so from various sources.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this is where the competent bodies had an interview with a person who resides in Skopje, since they believed that he was able to provide information. Is that what I read?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe I mentioned previously that OVR Cair is the relevant organisational unit and according to this document, they did undertake the activities which were their tasks to take, which are part of their responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, so, these measures described in the Official Note corroborate your evidence, that such measures are duties of the OVR on the territory of which the event took place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now please look at the document in tab 99.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P490.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
