utterances.text: You see that this is a report. On the second page, you see find the signature of the head of the OVR Cair, Ljube Krstevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And please read briefly the contents and tell me whether this report wrote by the head Krstevski corresponds to your knowledge of the events of that day.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the content is accurate and falls under the competencies of the OVR.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let's go back to an issue that we also started discussing already. When answering my question, you said that at one point in time OVR Cair requested assistance from the SVR regarding the accommodation and detention of the persons who were brought in and the paraffin glove tests, and that you appointed Milorad Bojic to assist OVR Cair with regards to the questions asked. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me whether Milorad Bojic had sufficient professional experience to be able to render expert assistance to OVR Cair?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. He is a very competent employee.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Milorad Bojic, the person who you appointed to assist the OVR Cair, inform you of any facts, problems, or anything related to the request of assistance that the head and the officers of the OVR Cair presented?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were certain problems; above all, problems related to keeping the people, the detention of these people. That is to say, OVR Cair did not have sufficient capacity for detained persons and that more police stations need to be included in order for them to be held in conditions that would enable work to be done with them. The number of persons that were brought in was also a problem. Also, a problem was the fact that, in a very short period of time, we have the right to detain persons for 24 hours. Therefore, in 24 hours, a lot of activities needed to be taken, especially from the forensic department, but I still believe that Mr. Bojic resolved this in a satisfactory manner. He established contact with the public prosecutor and investigating judge, asked their permission that we be allowed to detain these people until paraffin gloves were taken that were requested by OVR Cair. This was done during a working meeting at the premises of SVR Skopje. But another obligation stemmed from this working meeting, an obligation for OVR Cair, that the criminal report which they were planning to file against the persons that would -- in fact, we had information that the paraffin gloves had tested positive, and that this criminal report must be divided into three because the prosecutor and the investigating judge did not have the capacity to process all these people against whom criminal reports needed to be filed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please now look at the document in tab 104.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P262.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is an Official Note written by Toskovski Blagoja on the 17th of August, 2001, and the second paragraph reads: "On 13th of August, 2001, at around 1700 hours, at a meeting held in the premises of the SVR Skopje, OSOOK, in the presence of the chief of the OSOOK, Bojic Milorad, ZJO..." Does ZJO stand for the deputy prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Lazar Katrandziski, in the role of VD, that would mean acting; is that so?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the usual abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So acting deputy OJO stands for basic public prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The abbreviation OJO means basic public prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness and the counsel to pause and to avoid overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Reading this, I wanted you to clarify the abbreviations so that we know what they are about.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Acting basic public prosecutor and deputy public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Jovo Serafimovski, the following agreement was reached: "The detained individuals from the area of village of Ljuboten, where fighting occurred between the joint security forces against -- and terrorist groups, are to be held in police stations until the end of the entire preliminary procedure, due to the large number of detained individuals and shortage of time for completion of the entire procedure. "The investigating judge of Basic Court Skopje II, Bekir Sain [as interpreted], was informed of the recommendation and the agreement reached by the aforementioned deputies of the basic public prosecutor and the chief of the OSOOK at SVR Skopje. "A joint agreement was reached and confirmed with the investigating judge of Basic Court Skopje II, Bekir Sain, that the individuals are to be detained until the completion of the entire procedure." Mr. Stojanovski, with regards to this document, tell me, who was the only one who could approve that the persons who were brought in are held for longer than 24 hours, at the expiry of those 24 hours?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigating judge and the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when we are speaking about this procedure, was the judge who was informed about it, was he Bekir Sain, and do you know what was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe his name is Bekir Shahini, and I also believe he is of Albanian ethnicity. The translation, Shahini.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me whether this document reflects the information that you learned from Bojic Milorad at that time?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it does reflect it, but I cannot see that part about which I was informed pertaining to the division of the criminal report, separating them into three criminal reports, at the request of the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As we can see from this Official Note, also the active basic public prosecutor and one of the deputies to the public prosecutor were present?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering your testimony yesterday, did the police need to follow the instructions that it receives from the prosecutor or the judge in this specific case as well?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They're obligatory for us; however, allow me to correct myself. I think the agreement was struck later; that is to say, guidelines given by the public prosecutor, Vilma Ruskovska, in this area regarding the criminal report. I am speaking about the guidelines according to which OVR Cair later acted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And, tell me, who was in charge of filing the criminal reports?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the place where this event happened, OVR Cair.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And considering that from this note we can see that the investigating judge had already been informed and had been aware of the detained individuals, from your practice, then later, who had the competence over the detained individuals?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the moment when the investigating judge is included, he has full competence over the case, full responsibility over the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We discussed the competences of the police once it files a criminal report several times yesterday. And if I can interpret freely what you said several times, after that moment, the police only acts upon the order of either the prosecutor, who is requesting additional information, or the investigating judge, who already decided that an investigation would be open. Is this a summary of what you testified to several times yesterday? Is this a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the Macedonian language, the request for collecting certain information; however, this doesn't change the essence of what you have said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with all due respect, as you noticed this morning, I failed to finish within the planned time. I have some additional 45 minutes to one hour of questioning, so I kindly ask you to allow me to continue my direct examination on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're always warm and generous on Friday. We adjourn now for the weekend and resume at 9.00 on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 11th day of February, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.29 p.m.,
